profile.reading: BlockFusion operates a large cryptocurrency mining hosting and increasingly AI and high-performance-computing colocation campus at 5380 Frontier Avenue in Niagara Falls, New York, built on the site of a retired coal-burning power plant that the company converted into a data center campus. BlockFusion USA, Inc. was founded in 2019 by CEO Alex Martini-Lo Manto and COO Kant Trivedi, and operates this specific facility through a subsidiary called North East Data, LLC. The site draws roughly 90 percent of its power from carbon-free hydroelectric generation supplied by the nearby Robert Moses Niagara Hydroelectric Power Station, according to a 2022 SEC filing by one of its hosting customers, Bit Digital, Inc., a publicly traded Bitcoin mining company. A second major hosting customer, Gryphon Digital Mining, Inc., signed a colocation agreement with BlockFusion effective December 1, 2024, hosting nearly 5,000 mining machines on 12 megawatts of power for 156,000 dollars per month, replacing a prior hosting arrangement with a different provider, Coinmint, in Massena, New York. As of BlockFusion's most recent public disclosures, the Niagara Falls campus has 46 megawatts of Tier 1 power currently energized and operational, with more than 100 additional megawatts of Tier 3 capacity planned as part of a multi-year expansion developed with architecture and engineering firms Gensler, JB&B, and Thornton Tomasetti, reflecting the company's pivot from pure cryptocurrency mining hosting toward artificial intelligence and high-performance-computing colocation. In November 2025, BlockFusion announced plans to go public through a merger with a special-purpose acquisition company, Blue Acquisition Corp, becoming Blockfusion Data Centers, Inc. under ticker BLDC on Nasdaq, in a deal valuing the company at 450 million dollars pre-money with roughly 204 million dollars held in trust, a transaction still pending as of the most recent regulatory filing found. This specific OpenStreetMap record is one of eleven nearly identical points at this address, most plausibly representing separate structures within the same campus, since the underlying Gryphon colocation contract describes the site as including both mobile container-based mining units and indoor pod space within larger main buildings, a documented, phased-construction pattern consistent with multiple mapped structures rather than genuinely distinct campuses.

profile.research_note: This is one of 11 OSM points sharing the identical name "Blockfusion Niagra Falls" (OSM's own misspelling of Niagara) with no distinguishing addresses or codes, all at or near 5380 Frontier Avenue, Niagara Falls NY -- most plausibly representing multiple structures on a single BlockFusion campus rather than 11 genuinely separate facilities, documented explicitly here per this project's established handling of OSM duplicates. Blockfusion USA Inc, founded 2019 (CEO Alex Martini-Lo Manto, COO Kant Trivedi), converted a retired coal-burning power plant at this address into a cryptocurrency mining hosting and, increasingly, AI/HPC colocation data center, powered roughly 90% by carbon-free hydropower from the nearby Robert Moses Niagara Hydroelectric Power Station per a Bit Digital Inc SEC filing (Feb 2022). Operates via subsidiary North East Data LLC. Hosting customers per SEC filings: Bit Digital Inc (BTBT, as of 2022) and Gryphon Digital Mining Inc (GRYP, colocation agreement effective Dec 1 2024, hosting 4,969 miners on 12MW for $156,000/month, replacing a prior Coinmint LLC Massena NY arrangement). Company disclosed 46MW of Tier 1 power currently energized/operational plus 100+MW of Tier 3 capacity planned via a multi-year AI/HPC-focused expansion (targeting 200kW/rack density, developed with Gensler/JB&B/Thornton Tomasetti). As of Nov 19 2025, Blockfusion agreed to a SPAC merger with Blue Acquisition Corp/Cayman (BACC), to become Blockfusion Data Centers Inc, ticker BLDC, targeting Nasdaq, pre-money equity value $450M, ~$204M cash in trust, expected close H1 2026 (S-4 filed Dec 2025, amended through June 2026, deal still pending as of latest amendment found). The Gryphon colocation agreement describes the site as including both mobile container mining units and indoor "Pod" space within main buildings -- a sourced, plausible explanation for why OSM contributors mapped multiple separate structures at this one campus. Exact campus acreage, structure count, and the identity of the original coal plant were not found.

BlockFusion's Niagara Falls campus shows 0 MW of tracked power capacity, meaning either no public data exists for this facility or it operates below reporting thresholds.

The site sits on industrial land in Niagara Falls, a region with historically cheap hydroelectric power and a legacy of energy-intensive manufacturing. Local approval for the facility came in 2026. The research notes indicate a multi-building campus operating under the name Northeast Data LLC, with at least ten mapped structures clustered within 250 meters on the same Frontier Avenue property. The operator is tracked as BlockFusion.

The absence of a megawatt figure prevents any assessment of this facility's role in AI compute supply. It may be a small installation, a facility that does not report publicly, or a site where power allocation data remains unavailable. Without capacity data, the binding constraint framework cannot yet quantify how this location contributes to or competes for grid resources in New York State.

The research status is marked exhausted, meaning no additional public sources on power consumption or buildout timeline were found. Future updates would require either direct operator disclosure or regulatory filings specific to this site.
